citation: Koomen, M. J., Lock, C., Packer, D. M., Scolnik, R., Tousey, R., and Hulburt, E. O. (1952), Measurements of the Brightness of the Twilight Sky, Journal of the Optical Society of America 42(5), 353–356. doi:10.1364/JOSA.42.000353
screenshot: Local audit evidence: scratchpad/explore-twilight-altitude/references/koomen1952-page2.png; original PDF page 2 is the durable public source.
columns: Z=0 deg block, P=90 deg (zenith); H is solar altitude
transcription: Read visual raster, not OCR. Only selected rows with ordinary decimal notation are transcribed; no interpolation.
conversion: multiply by 10.7639 for cd m^-2, matching existing repository conversion

observations.high: Seven clear, cloudless, moonless evenings, May/June 1951

instrument: Green-filtered photomultiplier; 1.5 deg field of view; photopic response intended
uncertainty: No per-cell uncertainty provided. Tables are taken from smoothed curves through observations. Do not invent independent error bars or a pure altitude transfer law.
limitations: Different seasons and atmospheric transparency at the two stations
Solar-angle refraction convention is not explicit in the inspected description
No direct mapping from paired station ratio to a globally truncated standard atmosphere
